analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Benchmarking GS macro views vs. market pricing for 2027
key_insights: GS economists expect 2027 global real GDP growth of 2.8%, slightly above 2.7% in 2026, with risks tilted to the downside. Lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.

Inflation is expected to slow in 2027 as the impulse from US tariffs, energy and AI-related pressures fades. Economists expect only incremental tightening through early 2027 in most major economies, then gradual normalization cuts later in 2027.

Markets have repriced growth lower over the past few months. The RAI PC1 global growth factor dropped as cyclicals sold off relative to defensives, equities underperformed bonds and credit spreads widened.

The valuation reset in risky assets and a Risk Appetite Indicator still close to 0 imply a lower bar for risky assets to deliver positive returns if growth stays healthy next year. Both upside and downside tails remain possible.
GS baseline policy forecasts are more dovish than market pricing. The gap is widest for the ECB (normalisation cuts from 2027Q4), then the Fed, SNB and BoE, and narrowest for the BoJ.
Fed path: two 25bp hikes in Dec. 2026 and March 2027, followed by gradual cuts starting in Nov. 2027. BoE: only one hike, in February. BoJ: three 25bp hikes in Dec. 2026, March 2027 and June 2027.

On a risk-adjusted basis (GS 12m forecast vs. market pricing divided by implied vol), forecasts differ most from market pricing for CNY and BRL. FX team expects further CNY strength from strong exports, persistent undervaluation and policy support. BRL and COP are seen supported by high carry, tight policy and a more range-bound Dollar.
GS rates forecasts are below market pricing, especially for UK and US 2y yields. The rates team expects the largest 10y bond rallies in the US and UK, with the 2s10s Gilt curve steepening the most.
Strategists see the most equity upside relative to market pricing in US, EM and Japan, driven by slowing but healthy earnings growth.
Among commodities, the largest upside vs. futures is in Copper (AI and electrification demand against constrained supply) and Gold (structural central-bank buying and eventual Fed easing).
Three main risks to the baseline: higher energy prices from renewed Iran escalation, fiscal risks raising long-term yields, and AI capex disappointments.

Since October markets have become more worried about AI capex, with a rising implied probability of a further semiconductor sell-off. The implied probability of a further long-dated UST sell-off has eased, and the probability of a further oil rise is flat and below the March peak.

GOAL asset allocation: overweight equities, with OW US (S&P 500), OW Topix, UW Stoxx 600, neutral MXAPJ. Bonds: OW US, Germany and (12m) UK, UW Japan. Credit: OW USD IG and HY, UW EUR IG and HY. Gold OW, other commodities neutral.
Cross-asset valuation: S&P 500 forward P/E 18.2x (41st percentile of 10y history), Stoxx 600 14.1x (49th), MSCI EM 8.3x (0th). US 10y yield 5.2% is at the 99th percentile of its 10y range.
Vol: 3m ATM implied vol is 14.7 on the S&P 500 (51st percentile) against 22.3 one-month realised (85th percentile). Nikkei implied vol is 27.5 (94th percentile) and MSCI EM 26.1 (92nd).
earnings_insights: GS strategists expect slowing but healthy earnings growth to drive equity upside in the US, EM and Japan.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions. GS sees 2.8% global growth, easing inflation and a valuation reset that lowers the bar for risk assets.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher energy prices from renewed Iran escalation, fiscal risks raising long-term yields, and AI capex disappointments. Markets have repriced growth lower and the implied probability of a semiconductor sell-off has risen since October.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed escalation in Iran pushing energy prices higher, fiscal risks raising long-term yields, or AI capex growth disappointing would break the steady-growth baseline.
